text:
maria: Heads up — ap-southeast1 tiny-gpu pending jumped to ~120 around 03:12 UTC, mostly small batch jobs. Node utilization looks fine but scheduler shows many pods stuck Pending with '0/8 nodes' type messages.
alex: Did this follow the rack drain yesterday?
maria: yes — we decommissioned rack-7b at 02:50 for HW refresh, expected some churn but this looks like fragmentation not just capacity.
kevin: Can you paste the kubectl output for a couple of pending pods?
maria: sure, here's one sample:
```
NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
training-mini-87f5d        0/1     Pending   0          18m
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3m (x12 over 18m)  default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 5 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity, 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
kevin: pattern: nodeAffinity mismatch + taint mismatch. Are these pods requesting fractional GPUs (tiny)?
maria: yes requests: cpu 500m, gpu 0.125 (fractional via device plugin) + annotation redwood/incarn: mini.
tanya: Did the node label rollout from yesterday change gpu.flavor -> gpu.slab? I remember someone converting labels for rack-7b.
maria: confirmed — label rename ran in the rollout. Old affinity selectors still reference gpu.flavor values.
kevin: ah — scheduler can't match because label keys changed; K8s treats label key/value as exact. That causes pods to skip nodes even though capacity exists.
alex: ops-bot posted the drain plan but we missed converting a few workload templates. ops-bot: "Drain completed for rack-7b; 42 pods rescheduled"
sre-bot: Alert[FRAG-APSE1]: tiny-pod pending count > 100 for 6m.
tanya: Two parallel problems: label-key rename + new taint (quiet-maintenance) added to some nodes. Solutions: 1) quick reverse label-change on nodes, 2) patch deployment affinity to accept new label, 3) add toleration for quiet-maintenance for mini jobs.
kevin: For quick mitigation I'd prefer patching scheduler matching to accept legacy labels via topology-aware fallback (small code change). But shorter: mass-patch pods with annotation redwood/allow-label-fallback=true to tolerate both keys.
maria: I can run a kubectl patch on the deployments, but there are ~120 different jobs created by CI workers.
alex: Could we run a mutating webhook to add fallback tolerations/affinities for matching pods? That's heavier but automatic for new jobs.
tanya: I don't want to deploy a webhook during an already noisy window. Suggest two-step: 1) mass-patch the current queued pods (kubectl -n prod get pods -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl patch --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"redwood/quiet-maintenance","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]') 2) schedule a safe webhook rollout after stabilizing.
kevin: OK. Also we should reconcile node labels back to old key as fallback for 24h so older templates schedule. That is reversible.
maria: I'll run the toleration patch now on matching pending pods and also patch a canary deployment.
(30s later)
maria: Patch applied to 102 pending pods, observed 78 start evicting from pending -> scheduling -> running. CPU stable, GPUs allocated.
kevin: Nice. Can we also snapshot scheduler debug logs to ensure no other constraint is blocking?
maria: attached snippet from scheduler logs: 
```
I0330 03:15:24.123 scheduler: binding pod training-mini to node gpu-apse1-33
I0330 03:15:25.789 scheduler: predicate failed: NodeAffinityMismatch for pod training-small
```
alex: Action items: maria -> run mass toleration patch + reconcile node labels for 24h (in progress). kevin -> draft small scheduler fallback PR to accept either label key (low-risk). tanya -> own webhook design and rollout plan after incident.
ops-bot: Incident ticket #INC-9832 created: ap-southeast1 tiny-pod fragmentation.
maria: quick cost note — keeping fallback labels on for 24h will slightly increase cross-az binpacking but avoids hundreds of failed job retries which cost more. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
kevin: +1. let's revert labels after 24h and merge scheduler fix in canary.
maria: will follow up with a short postmortem in #postmortems and add a prompt template to infra runbook for label-rollouts.
tanya: thanks all. :thumbsup:
